thesis: Profitable FX-neutral growth supports business merit, while the substantive content-cash bridge is missing to both advocates. Neither an absence of earnings surprise nor an adverse chart proves business failure, and neither profitability nor guidance establishes buying value. Neutral reflects this unresolved owner-return gate.
strongest_counterexample: Revenue grew13% and12% FX-neutral with33% operating margin, giving a strong present earnings base that does not require a surprise catalyst.
invalidation_conditions: A complete comparable content/debt cash reconciliation shows owner cash after obligations above zero and delivery of at least the issuer31.5% annual operating-margin forecast, resolving major earnings-to-cash gates.
A subsequent comparable FX-neutral revenue growth rate at or below zero with margin below the issuer31.5% annual forecast would invalidate the retained profitable-growth scenario.
evidence_gaps: Sustainable owner cash and competitive economics.
Matched cash valuation and actual annual guidance delivery.
decisive_factors: Current growth and margin are observed; annual forecast remains prospective.
Content accounting profitability is not owner cash.
Negative MACD and below both averages provide no confirmed bottom.
